claims.Proposed claim: Corruption augmentation improves robustness to historical dropout
claims.Required limitation: Synthetic missingness on simulated telemetry; clean targets; three seeds

claims.Proposed claim: An explicit availability mask improves on augmentation (C better than B)
claims.Required limitation: Zero fill is itself an exact missingness cue (no natural exact zeros); C seed 33 is an epoch-3 checkpoint

claims.Proposed claim: The model warns of failures early (24 h)
claims.Quantitative evidence: A: recall 0.20 ± 0.05 vs chance 0.19 ± 0.00, lift 1.67 ± 0.36x; B: recall 0.06 ± 0.01 vs chance 0.18 ± 0.00, lift 0.32 ± 0.06x; C: recall 0.13 ± 0.01 vs chance 0.19 ± 0.00, lift 0.91 ± 0.09x; 98 eligible episodes
claims.Required limitation: Score available only after target_end; 6 h resolution; alerts are not diagnoses; few episodes

claims.Proposed claim: Surprise flags the onset of pre-failure shifts (secondary 48 h horizon)
claims.Quantitative evidence: A: recall 0.93 ± 0.02 vs chance 0.35 ± 0.01; B: recall 0.60 ± 0.00 vs chance 0.32 ± 0.00; C: recall 0.91 ± 0.04 vs chance 0.35 ± 0.00; median lead 43 h; 97 eligible episodes
claims.Can we state it?: Only as a secondary, exploratory observation (no frozen claim rule covers 48 h)
claims.Required limitation: Post hoc: the simulator injects a step in the failing component's sensor 48 h before failure; not realistic degradation

claims.Quantitative evidence: Stage 3/4 predefined criteria met by all nine selected checkpoints (effective rank >= 16, every latent std >= 0.1)
claims.Can we state it?: Yes, as non-collapse by the predefined criteria
claims.Required limitation: Model C has lower effective rank (25.2, 23.6, 16.7); no physical semantics claimed
